title: DVR localizations of normalization in a finite field extension
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a nonzero local integral domain of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D\ne0$. Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field], with $D\subseteq K=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ (each element of $K$ is a ratio of elements of $D$ with nonzero denominator), and suppose $[L:K]<\infty$. Let $C\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $C$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] of Krull dimension $1$, and its given inclusion in $L$ makes $L$ its fraction field. There exists a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset C$ with $\mathfrak q\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$. Every such prime $\mathfrak q$ is nonzero and maximal. For every such $\mathfrak q$, the localization $A=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] embeds into $L$ by $c/s\mapsto c/s$, and its image is the subring $\{c/s\in L:c,s\in C,\ s\notin\mathfrak q\}$. This subring is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] containing $D$, with fraction field $L$, and its maximal ideal satisfies $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak qA$, $\mathfrak m_A\cap C=\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$. No separability assumption is imposed on $L/K$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final proof paragraph: integral closure, lying over and localization; Tag 09IG, algebra-lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind. Expanded construction in the parent's former steps 5--8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres] to $D$, $K$, $L$: $D$ is Noetherian of dimension $1$ and $L/K$ is finite, so $C$ is a Noetherian normal domain of dimension $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] to the same inclusions to obtain that the given $C\subseteq L$ makes $L$ its fraction field. These results impose neither normality on $D$ nor separability on $L/K$.

The inclusion $D\hookrightarrow C$ is integral by the definition of integral closure. Lying over [pqf-lem-lying-over] supplies a prime $\mathfrak q$ with $\mathfrak q\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$. For any such prime, choose $0\ne d\in\mathfrak m_D$; its image is nonzero in $C$ and belongs to $\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\ne0$. It is maximal: otherwise a maximal ideal strictly containing it would give the prime chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak n$, contradicting $\dim C=1$.

Fix any such $\mathfrak q$. Since $C$ is Noetherian, normal and one-dimensional and $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] makes $A=C_{\mathfrak q}$ a DVR. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] with $S=C\setminus\mathfrak q$ and fraction field $L$: it gives the injective map $A\to L$, $c/s\mapsto c/s$, and fraction field $L$. Its image is exactly the displayed set of fractions, since every element of $A$ is represented by such a pair and every such pair defines an element of $A$. The image contains $D$ by $d\mapsto d/1$.

By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qA$. Its contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak q$ by [lem-trf-localization-maximal-contraction]. Contraction through the composite $D\hookrightarrow C\hookrightarrow A$ is therefore $\mathfrak q\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$. These equalities also hold for the embedded image in $L$, since the embedding is injective.

Step 1: 09IG (lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres) needs only a Noetherian 1-dimensional domain and a finite L/K, and the Mathlib-leaf fraction-field node gives Frac C = L, so no normality of D or separability of L/K is used. Step 2: lying over applies to D→C, which is injective and integral. Every q over m_D is nonzero because it contains a nonzero d in m_D. It is maximal because (0)⊊q⊊n would contradict dim C = 1. Step 3: the Dedekind-localization leaf at a maximal q gives a DVR, and the normal-localization leaf with S = C∖q gives the injective map into L and Frac = L. Step 4: the localization def gives m_A = qA, the localization contraction leaf gives m_A∩C = q, and composing gives m_A∩D = m_D. proof_deps equal the union of uses. Edge cases checked: ramified Z_(2)⊂Z[i], non-normal k[t^2,t^3] with L = K, purely inseparable F_p[t]_(t)⊂K(t^{1/p}), and several primes over m_D. The statement matches what the parent lem-sfb-local-domain-fg-field-dvr step 3 uses. Duplicate search (integral closure / DVR / Krull-Akizuki) found no restatement. There is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply.
